Introduction

Seven ways to say: there's a game near you, and it's on right now.

What ARENA is

A mobile platform that makes local sport easy to find, book, play and share. Players see courts near them and who's playing right now; venues fill their slots, run tournaments and earn a Verified badge.

What's inside

Seven identity directions: two wordmarks, four symbols and one integrated lockup. Each is drawn on a grid, checked down to favicon size, and comes with its own system: three circle modes, three lockups and six status poses.

How to choose

Read each direction as a whole: its idea, its system, then the mockups. Finish on the side-by-side pages. Pick one, or name two you'd like to see combined.

Foundations
The brief

Purpose, positioning, attributes and the ideas each direction grew from.

The brief
Purpose

Get more people playing, by making every local arena discoverable, bookable and alive.

Positioning

The home of local sport: where players find the game and venues fill their slots. ARENA shows what's live now, runs the competition and vouches for the venue.

Attributes

Live · Competitive · Communal · Trusted · Local with global ambition · Effortless · Energetic but premium.

Personality

The confident captain: organises the game, knows every court, keeps it fair, isn't loud about it.

The tension

Street-court energy against a trusted, premium platform. The mark stays calm and engineered; motion, photography and one live accent carry the noise.

What to avoid

Green pitch rectangles, balls, swooshes, neon on black, generic pins, triangle As, flags. The place itself (bowl, ring, court) is the richer idea.

Directions
Seven directions

Two wordmarks, four symbols and one integrated lockup.

Direction 01 · Wordmark
Court Lines

ARENA drawn with the court's own geometry: the A is the trapezoid key, its crossbar the free-throw line; the E's middle arm floats free like a painted lane line.

Court Lines system
Three circle modes · three lockups · six status poses
Direction 02 · Wordmark
Match Day

Poster-weight extended lowercase in Syne ExtraBold: loud like a match-day poster. Each a has its counter filled and a location pin carved into the optical centre of the bowl; both a's match, so the word reads clean and symmetrical around the pins.

Match Day system
Three circle modes · three lockups · six status poses
Direction 03 · Symbol + mascot
Pixel Scoreboard

A square-pixel pin mascot lit like a stadium LED scoreboard, with six poses that are the app's own statuses (available, live, booked, closed, fully booked, ask).

Pixel Scoreboard system
Three circle modes · three lockups · six status poses
Direction 04 · Symbol
Live Pin

A map pin whose head is a stadium seen from above (the racetrack shape geometry literally calls a 'stadium'), with a live light switched on at its shoulder: there's a game near you, and it's on now.

Live Pin system
Three circle modes · three lockups · six status poses
Direction 05 · Symbol
Convergence Crest

A tournament bracket (four entrants, two semis, one final) carved into a shield: everyone meets here, the path resolves to one winner, and the venue is verified.

Convergence Crest system
Three circle modes · three lockups · six status poses
Direction 06 · Integrated lockup
Pin in the A

The first A's counter is a map pin standing on the A's crossbar (find); the last A's counter holds the live light (play). Find it, then it's on: one word, the whole product.

Pin in the A system
Three circle modes · three lockups · six status poses
Direction 07 · Symbol
Centre Light

The centre circle seen from the floodlight gantry: two halves split by the halfway line, gathered around the spot where every game starts, and the spot is lit.

Centre Light system
Three circle modes · three lockups · six status poses
